summary: Tampalawela Dhammaratana is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Sunethradevi Pirivena, the University of Kelaniya, the University of Paris under Jean-François Lyotard, Paris-Sorbonne University under Michel Hulin, and completed postdoctoral studies at École Pratique des Hautes Études under Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat.

Tan Chung is a historian and sinologist who earned his PhD from Visva-Bharati University. He held positions at the National Defence Academy, University of Delhi, Jawaharlal Nehru University, Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts, and the Institute of Chinese Studies.

Tan Poh Beng is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed an MA at the International Buddhist College under Charles Willemen and Tilak Kariyawasam, and also studied under teachers Sumanasiri and Shengshou.
Tan Sitong was a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied under Wang Zhengyi and Yang Renshan.

Tan Yun-shan was a scholar of sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Wenjiang Shuyuan, Mijiang Academy, Hunan Normal University, and Chuanshan Academy, later teaching at Lida Academy and serving as Professor of Chinese Studies at Visva-Bharati University.
Tandin Dorji is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Tibetology. He has served as a history lecturer at Sherubtse College and as a lecturer at the National Institute of Education, Paro.

Tanero Sasakawa was a scholar of sinology, history, archaeology, and Japanology. After studying at the University of Tokyo from approximately 1893 to 1896, he held posts at Toyo University and Meiji University.

Tansen Sen is a historian, sinologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Peking University and the University of Pennsylvania, the latter under Victor H. Mair. He later held an academic post at Baruch College.
Tanso Hirose was a scholar of sinology and philosophy. He studied at Kamei Juku from around 1797 to 1801 under Hodō and later founded the Kangien academy in 1801.

Tanzan Hara was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Yushima Seido and Shoheizaka Gakumonjo. He served in the Ministry of Religion, as a professor at the University of Tokyo, and as superintendent of Komazawa University.

Tao Jiang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his PhD at Temple University under Shigenori Nagatomo. He served as an associate professor in the Department of Religion at Rutgers University.
Tao Jin is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. He completed his PhD at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign in 2008 under doctoral supervisor Alexander L. Mayer.
Tao Pan is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He earned a BA from Fudan University in 2010 and completed a Magister Artium at the University of Munich.
Tarab Tulku was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts as a curator at the Royal Danish Library around 1967 and worked at the University of Copenhagen.

Taranatha Tarkavachaspati was an Indologist and linguist. He served as Professor of Grammar and Philosophy at Sanskrit College and University from approximately 1845 to 1873 and as Professor of Sanskrit at Benares Sanskrit College.

Tarthang Tulku is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He taught at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University from 1963 to 1968, headed the Tibetan Nyingma Meditation Center, and founded the Nyingma Institute, where he served as Head Lama.

Taryo Makita was a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar. Educated at Bukkyo, Otani, and Kyoto universities, he held faculty posts at Kyoto University, Gifu University of Education, Gifu Shotoku Gakuen University, and served as president of Saitama Institute of Technology.
Tashi Densapa is a scholar in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He served as editor of the Bulletin of Tibetology and was attested as director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology in 2008.

Tashi Tsering is a Tibetologist, historian, and linguist. Educated at the Central School for Tibetans, he worked at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives, directed the Amnye Machen Institute, and held a professorship at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

Tatiana Oranskaia is an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Saint Petersburg and Kendriya Hindi Sansthan. She held academic posts at the University of Saint Petersburg (1973–1998) and served as a professor at the University of Hamburg (1998–2016).
